# Part {-}: Brief description of the sample

This first part is dedicated to a description of the sample.

## Main characteristics of the dataset

### Total sample

`r data_tot_clean %>% nrow()` surveys have been completed overall. Responses with no contact information or from undocumented mothers were excluded, for ethical reasons for the latter.

## Brief description of the participants included

Over the `r data_full %>% nrow()` remaining participants,

-   `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow()*100, digit = 2)` % are Low-SES (i.e., no tertiary education) (N=`r data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow()`).

-   `r round(data_full %>% filter(ECSUsed == "Non") %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % have never used ECS (N=`r data_full %>% filter(ECSUsed == "Non") %>% nrow()`)

-   Single mothers: `r round(data_full %>% filter(SingleMum == TRUE) %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % (N =`r data_full %>% filter(SingleMum == TRUE) %>% nrow()`). Mothers were recruited between their fourth and ninth months of pregnancy.

-   Primparae: `r round(data_full %>% filter(Primipare == TRUE) %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % (N =`r data_full %>% filter(Primipare == TRUE) %>% nrow()`)

-   Digital divide: More than a third (`r round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ComputerYN == "Non") %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow())*100, 1)`%) of low-SES respondents don't have access to a computer compared to `r round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & ComputerYN == "Non") %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>% nrow())*100, 1)`% for High-SES respondents. Similarly, one third (`r round((data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" & ComputerYN == "Non") %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else") %>% nrow())*100, 1)`%) of mothers born abroad don't have access to a computer compared to `r round((data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "French" & ComputerYN == "Non") %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "French") %>% nrow())*100, 1)`% for non-migrants.

## Main variables

### Age

The age of the participants follows a normal distribution:

```{r Age, fig.cap= "Median and Mean Age of mothers in the sample (mean in red on the figure)"}
MeanAge = data_full %>% summarize(mean = mean(Age), median = median(Age))

regulartable(data_full %>% summarize(Mean = round(mean(Age), 1), Median = median(Age))) %>% 
  autofit()


data_full %>% 
ggplot(aes(Age))+
geom_density()+
  geom_vline(data = MeanAge, aes(xintercept=mean, color = "red"), show.legend = FALSE)+ scale_fill_discrete(guide="none")

```

### Level of education of the mothers

`r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow()/data_full %>% nrow()*100, digit = 2)` % of Low-SES (i.e., no tertiary education) (N=`r data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow()`).

```{r education, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5, fig.cap= "Distribution of the level of education of mothers in the sample"}

ggplot(data_full, aes(OrderedEduc, fill = OrderedEduc), colour = cbPalette)+
  geom_bar()+
  labs( x = "Level of education of the mother")+
  labs(fill = "Mother's level of educ.", size = 20)
```

## Childcare plans after birth

Parents wanting to use an ECS are over-represented in the sample: `r round(data_full %>% filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use them.

```{r GraphMig, fig.cap= "Childcare plan after birth of mothers in the sample"}
data_full %>% 
ggplot(aes(ECSPlanTo, fill = ECSPlanTo), colour = cbPalette)+
  geom_bar()+
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("No", "Yes"))+
  labs( x = "Want to use ECS", fill = "Want to use ECS")+scale_fill_manual(values = cbPalette, labels = c( "No", "Yes"))


```

### Analysis for low-SES

Among low-SES parents, parents wanting to use an ECS are still over-represented in the sample: `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use them compared to `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % for the high-SES parents The same holds for migrant families: `r round(data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else") %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use ECS among them. Even more interestingly, even among inactive parents, parents wanting to use an ECS are still over-represented in the sample: `r round(data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive") %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % of inactive mothers want to use ECS.

## Sensitivity analyses: robustness across several definitions of Socio-Economic Status

### Education level of the mother

Mothers with tertiary education are more likely to want ECS from about 14 percentage points.

```{r IntentionBinaryEduc, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by binary level of education of the mother"}

data_full%>%
  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=Educ),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = Educ, y = Intention1or0*1000, color = Educ),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
xlab("Level of education of the mother (Bac = no tertiary education)") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle =45 , hjust = 1, vjust = 1))

```

Here is the table for three simple regression models:

1.  the first one estimates probability to intend to use ECS by mothers' level of education as a binary outcome (having a tertiary education or not).

2.  the second one is the same model, but with strata fixed effects (MaternityWardXWave)

3.  the third one is the same as 2., but controlling with a dummy for whether mothers are active (i.e. employed, student, etc.) or not.

```{r ModelEducIntention, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}


IntentionSES        <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ Educ , data = data_full) 
IntentionSESFE      <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ Educ | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
IntentionSESActFE   <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ Educ + Active | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave)  
IntentionSESActBPFE   <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ Educ + Active + BirthPlace4 | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave)  
IntentionSESActmigFE   <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ Educ + Active + BirthPlace4 + COM | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave)  
 

 modelsummary(list(
"(Intention to use ECS by education level (dummy no tertiary education))"                                            = IntentionSES, 
"Intention to use ECS by education level (dummy no tertiary education) with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"      = IntentionSESFE, 
"Intention to use ECS by education level and Activity with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"                       = IntentionSESActFE,
"(4)"                       = IntentionSESActBPFE,
"(5)"                       = IntentionSESActmigFE




), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave"),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Intention to use ECS by Education level binary",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)

```

There is still an effect of the level of education after controlling for whether the mother is currently active, but most of the effect of the level of education seem to go through the activity status of the mother.The R2 of the simple model with no control is quite low, but double by including mothers' activity status.

For a more fine-grained analysis, we can break down the level of education of mothers in the sample in smaller categories:

```{r graphEducDetailedIntention, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by binary level of education of the mother"}


data_full%>%
  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=OrderedEduc),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = OrderedEduc, y = Intention1or0*1000, color = Educ),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
xlab("Level of education of the mother ") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))
```

The 9-11 category's unexpected boost might be explained by the fact that these mothers are nearly exclusively from Sub-Saharan Africa and thus very favorable to ECS (see below, to be explored in more details).

The coefficient table of the linear regression with the detailed level of education is currently hard to interpret:

```{r ModelEducOrderedIntention, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

#library(sjlabelled)

# Run regression analyses with explicit level labels

### Migration background of the mother

Mothers that are born is France are slightly more likely to want ECS compared to mothers born abroad. However, the difference is very small. Interestingly, there seems to be an interaction between the level of education and the migration background of the mother that will be explored in subsequent analyses.

```{r, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by binary migration background of the mother"}


data_full%>%
  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=FrenchYN),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = FrenchYN, y = Intention1or0*1000, color = Educ),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
    stat_summary(aes(x = FrenchYN, y = Intention1or0*1000),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975))) +
xlab("Migration background of the mother") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle =45 , hjust = 1, vjust = 1))


```

Here is the table for first three simple regression models:

1.  the first one estimates probability to intend to use ECS by mothers' migration background as a binary outcome (being born in a French territory or not).

2.  the second one is the same model, but with strata fixed effects (MaternityWardXWave).

3.  the third model is the same as 2., but also including mothers' activity at the time of the interview. Note that as Activity may be considered as a collider (it is influenced both by SES and ECS use), we should not control for it in our regressions. 3. is just for exploratory purposes.

```{r ModelMigIntention, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

IntentionMig                <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ FrenchYN , data = data_full) 
IntentionMigFE              <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
IntentionMigActFE           <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ FrenchYN + Active| blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave)
 

 modelsummary(list(
  "Intention to use ECS by migration background"                                                          = IntentionMig, 
  "Intention to use ECS by migration with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"                             = IntentionMigFE, 
  "Intention to use ECS by migration and activity with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)"                = IntentionMigActFE
), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave"),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Number of ECS Known (KnownNbTypeECS)",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)

```

We can see than the difference between mothers born in France and others is very small (less than 1 percentage point), but significant. The dummy created for whether the mother comes from Asia or MENA seems to be more meaningfull in terms of  When we introduce mothers' activity at the time of the interview, the effect of migration background disappears. The R2 of these models are even smaller than the ones for the level of education.

We can break down the migration background into more meaningful categories: birth regions.

The difference seems to be meaningful: mothers born in MENA or Asia are on average less favorable to ECS than others, but, as for mothers born in France, there is also a socio-economic gradient of ECS use intention within the category of mothers born in these regions. The effect of education is stronger for mothers from MENA, Asia or France than for people born in other countries. For the latter, education barely seem to play a role.

## Timing of ECS wanted

```{r }

library(data.table)

# Convert data_full to a data.table
setDT(data_full)

# Create an empty binary variable
data_full[, ECSDateBinary := NA_character_]

# Define the cutoff date
cutoff_date <- as.Date("2023-09-02")

# Set values for ECS dates before and after the cutoff
data_full[ECSDate < cutoff_date, ECSDateBinary := "Before 09.2023"]
data_full[ECSDate >= cutoff_date, ECSDateBinary := "After 09.2023"]


chisq.test(data_full$Educ, data_full$ECSDateBinary)


```

High-SES mothers tend to put their child significantly earlier in ECS (X-squared = 16.377, df = 1, p-value = 5.191e-05). For instance, `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & ECSDateBinary == "Before 09.2023") %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100`% of high-SES mothers want to put their child in ECS in September 2023 or before, while it is the case for only `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSDateBinary == "Before 09.2023") %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow(), digit = 1)*100`% low-SES mothers. Of course, this decision is likely to have heavy consequences for an effective access to ECS as most of the places are allocated around June for September.

## Type of childcare wanted

Among parents wanting to use an ECS, those wanting *crèches* (daycare centers) are over-represented: `r round(data_full %>% filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE & WantCreche == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use them (`r round(data_full %>% filter( WantCreche == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % on the general population).

```{r}
   

data_full %>% 
  filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% 
ggplot(aes(ECSType7, fill = ECSType7), colour = cbPalette)+
  geom_bar()+
  labs( x = "Type of early childcare wanted for the child", fill = "")+
coord_flip()


```

### Analysis for low-SES

Again, the pattern is quite similar if we restrict the analyses to low-SES mothers: `r round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" &  WantCreche == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE ) %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use daycare. The same holds for migrant families: `r round(data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" &  WantCreche == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE ) %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` % want to use them. Even more interestingly, even among inactive parents, the proportion wanting to use daycare is still quite high and the pattern is the same: `r  round(data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" &  WantCreche == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE ) %>%  nrow(), digit = 1)*100` %. Only the drop-in daycare (halte-garderies) has a slightly higher proportion compared to the general population, but the increase is very modest: `r round((data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" & WantHG == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive" & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() *100 ) - (data_full %>% filter(WantHG == TRUE & ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow() / data_full %>% filter(ECSPlanTo == TRUE) %>% nrow()*100), digit = 1)` percentage points.

```{r, fig.width = 40, fig.height = 30}

   
data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive") %>% 
ggplot(aes(ECSType7, fill = ECSType7), colour = cbPalette)+
  geom_bar()+
  labs( x = "Type of early childcare wanted for the child for inactive mothers", fill = "", size = 20)+ theme(text=element_text(size=50))


```

This raises the question of the types of ECS than are known by mothers. Maybe crèches is the only structure they know of.

# Part {-}: Information dynamics

## Number of ECS known

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Mean number of ECS known for the general population 
 meanECSKnownTotalPop = round(mean(data_full$KnownNbTypeECS), 2)

# Mean for high-SES
meanECSKnownHighSES = round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownLowSES = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)), 1) 

# Mean for low-SES
meanECSKnownLowSES = round(data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownLowSES = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)), 1) 


# Mean for migrant
meanECSKnownMigrant = round(data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownMig = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)), 1)

# Mean for Non Mig
meanECSKnownNonMig = round(data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "French") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownNonMigr = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)),1)


# Mean for inactive
meanECSKnownInactive = round(data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Inactive") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownInactive = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)),1)

# Mean for Active mothers
meanECSKnownActive = round(data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Active") %>%  summarize( MeanECSKnownActiv = mean(KnownNbTypeECS)), 1)



```

First, low-SES mothers knew on average significantly less ECS types than their more affluent counterparts. When asked to tell us all the ECS type they knew, mothers knew `r meanECSKnownTotalPop` ECS types on average. But while high-SES mothers knew on average `r meanECSKnownHighSES` ECS types, low-SES mothers knew on average `r meanECSKnownLowSES` of them (t = -13.2, p-value \< 2.2e-16).

This is even more true for migrants mothers that knew `r meanECSKnownMigrant` ECS types on average regardless of their socio-economic background (t = -18.845, p-value \< 2.2e-16) and for inactive mothers (M inactive = `r meanECSKnownInactive`). This effect is still significant after controlling for activity and education level. Therefore, while migration background doesn't seem to affect ECS intention much, it may play a significant role in information dynamics.

```{r tbleNumberECSKnownSES, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

# Regressions Number of ECS Known (KnownNbTypeECS)

NumberECSKnownEduc          <- feols(KnownNbTypeECS ~ Educ, data = data_full) 
NumberECSKnownEducFE        <- feols(KnownNbTypeECS ~ Educ | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
NumberECSKnownMigFE         <- feols(KnownNbTypeECS ~ FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave)
NumberECSKnownActivityFE    <- feols(KnownNbTypeECS ~ Active | blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave)
NumberECSKnownEducMigFE     <- feols(KnownNbTypeECS ~ Educ + FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave)
#NumberECSKnownEducMigActFE  <- feols(KnownNbTypeECS ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Activity | blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
NumberECSKnownEducXMigFE    <- feols( KnownNbTypeECS ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Educ*FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 
#NumberECSKnownEducXMigActFE <- feols( KnownNbTypeECS ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Active + Educ*FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~blocksMatWave) 


 modelsummary(list(
   "Number of ECS Known by education level "                                        = NumberECSKnownEduc,
   "Number of ECS Known by education level with Fixed Effects (MaternityWard^Wave)" = NumberECSKnownEducFE, 
   "Number of ECS Known by migration status with FE"                                = NumberECSKnownMigFE, 
 #  "Number of ECS Known by mother's activity status with FE"                        = NumberECSKnownActivityFE, 
   "Number of ECS Known by educ and mig with FE"                                    = NumberECSKnownEducMigFE,
 #  "Number of ECS Known by educ and mig and activity with FE"                       = NumberECSKnownEducMigActFE,
   "Number of ECS Known with interaction EducXMig and FE"                           = NumberECSKnownEducXMigFE
), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave"),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Number of ECS Known (KnownNbTypeECS)",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)

```

## Types of ECS known

```{r, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}
# Proportion of low SES that know only creche
PropKnowOnlyCrecheLowSES = round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & KnowsCrecheOnly == TRUE ) %>% nrow()/ data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac") %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of high SES that know only creche
PropKnowOnlyCrecheHighSES = round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & KnowsCrecheOnly == TRUE ) %>% nrow()/ data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup") %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of migrant that know only creche
PropKnowOnlyCrecheMig = round((data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else" & KnowsCrecheOnly == TRUE ) %>% nrow()/ data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "Else") %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of non migrant that know only creche
PropKnowOnlyCrecheNonMig = round((data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "French"& KnowsCrecheOnly == TRUE ) %>% nrow()/ data_full %>% filter(FrenchYN == "French") %>% nrow())*100, 1)


# Proportion of active mothers that know only creche
PropKnowOnlyCrecheActive = round((data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Active" & KnowsCrecheOnly == TRUE ) %>% nrow()/ data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Active") %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of inactive mothers that know only creche
PropKnowOnlyCrecheInactive = round((data_full %>% filter(Act3 != "Active" & KnowsCrecheOnly == TRUE ) %>% nrow()/ data_full %>% filter(Act3 !="Active") %>% nrow())*100, 1)


# Proportion of active mothers that know only creche
PropKnowHGActive = round((data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Active" & KnowsHG == TRUE ) %>% nrow()/ data_full %>% filter(Act3 == "Active") %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of inactive mothers that know only creche
PropKnowHGInactive = round((data_full %>% filter(Act3 != "Active" & KnowsHG == TRUE ) %>% nrow()/ data_full %>% filter(Act3 !="Active") %>% nrow())*100, 1)
                                                                

```



Not only low-SES mothers knew less ECS types than high-SES mothers did, but low-SES mothers were significantly more likely to know Crèches and only Crèches (% low-SES = `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheLowSES` , % high-SES = `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheHighSES` ). This is also true for migrant mothers, that were even more likely to be in this situation than low-SES mothers (% migrants = `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheMig`), while only `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheNonMig` % of native mothers were in this situation.

Strikingly, it was also the case for inactive mothers: `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheInactive` % of them only knew the crèches, while it was the case for `r PropKnowOnlyCrecheActive` % of active mothers. This even though generally, inactive mothers are less likely to access a place in crèche because they don't work. Besides, inactive mothers are just as likely to know Halte-garderies compared to active mothers. Only `r PropKnowHGInactive` %  of them knew this type of structure, while this is one type of care created for them.


Interestingly, looking at the coefficients of the regressions, whether the mother is active is contributing to a lesser extent than Education level and Migration background:

```{r, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

# Probability to know only crèche


CrecheOEduc             <- feols(KnowsCrecheOnly ~ Educ, data = data_full)
CrecheOEducFE           <- feols(KnowsCrecheOnly ~ Educ | blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )
CrecheOMig              <- feols(KnowsCrecheOnly ~ FrenchYN, data = data_full)
CrecheOMigFE            <- feols(KnowsCrecheOnly ~ FrenchYN | blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )
CrecheOMigEducMatFE     <- feols(KnowsCrecheOnly ~ Educ + FrenchYN | blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )
CrecheOMigEducMatActFE  <- feols(KnowsCrecheOnly ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Active | blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )
CrecheOMigXEducFE       <- feols( KnowsCrecheOnly ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Educ*FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
#CrecheOMigXEducActFE    <- feols( KnowsCrecheOnly ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Educ*FrenchYN + Active| blocksMatWave, data = data_full,cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )



modelsummary(list(
"Knows Only Crèche by Educ level" = CrecheOEduc,
"Knows Only Crèche by Educ level with Fixed Effects" = CrecheOEducFE,
"Knows Only Crèche by Migration status " = CrecheOMig,     
"Knows Only Crèche by Migration status with Fixed Effects " = CrecheOMigFE,     
"Knows Only Crèche by Educ level control Mig with Fixed Effects" = CrecheOMigEducMatFE,
"Knows Only Crèche by Educ level control Mig and activity with Fixed Effects" = CrecheOMigEducMatActFE,
"Knows Only Crèche interaction MigxEduc with Fixed Effects" = CrecheOMigXEducFE
), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs",  "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave" ),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Probability to know only crèche",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)
                                                      

```

The interaction between the level of education and migration background is significant, along with all the other variables of the regressions.

### Relationship between knowing only crèches and intention

Knowing only crèche does not seem to contribute much to the intention to use ECS (see \@ref(Appendix 2) for the detailed regression table). If anything, mothers born in France are slightly less likely to want to use ECS if they know only crèche (the interaction is significant, p = 0.004).

```{r GraphIntentionKOnlyCrecgeEduc, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by knowing only crèche and SES"}

  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%

## Cost of crèche

```{r, echo = FALSE}

# Proportion of ppl not knowing at all the cost of ECS (= answering "don't know" when asked) on the general population   
CostNSP = round((data_full %>% filter(AffordCostDK == TRUE) %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of ppl not knowing at all the cost of ECS (= answering "don't know" when asked) among ppl that have never used ECS
CostNSPNU = round((data_full %>% filter(ECSUsed == "Non" & AffordCostDK == TRUE) %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>% filter(ECSUsed == "Non") %>%  nrow())*100, 1)


# Proportion of Low-SES ppl not knowing at all the cost of ECS (= answering "don't know" when asked) among ppl that have never used ECS
PropNSPCostLow = round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSUsed == "Non" & AffordCostDK == TRUE) %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>%  filter(Educ == "Bac" & ECSUsed == "Non") %>% nrow())*100, 1)

# Proportion of High-SES ppl not knowing at all the cost of ECS (= answering "don't know" when asked) among ppl that have never used ECS
PropNSPCostHigh =round((data_full %>% filter(Educ == "Sup" & ECSUsed == "Non" & AffordCostDK == TRUE) %>% nrow()) / (data_full %>%  filter(Educ == "Sup" & ECSUsed == "Non") %>% nrow())*100, 1)



```

Relatively few people had an idea of what the cost of childcare is (regardless of whether this idea is accurate or not): `` `r CostNSP` ``% of parents couldn't tell us anything about the price of childcare (`` `r CostNSPNU` ``% of parents that have never used ECS). Low-SES mothers were significantly less likely to have an idea of the costs of a place, even if we restrict the analyses only to the ones that have never used ECS: the proportion were `` `r PropNSPCostLow` ``% for low-SES mothers, compared to `` `r PropNSPCostHigh` ``% for high-SES mothers.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Do the linear models

# Do the linear models


AffordCostDKEduc                    <- feols(AffordCostDK ~ Educ, data = data_full)
AffordCostDKEducFE                  <- feols(AffordCostDK ~ Educ | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)    
AffordCostDKMig                     <- feols(AffordCostDK ~ FrenchYN, data = data_full)
AffordCostDKMigFE                   <- feols(AffordCostDK ~ FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)    
AffordCostDKEducMigFE               <- feols(AffordCostDK ~ Educ + FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
AffordCostDKEducEveruUsedECSFE      <- feols(AffordCostDK ~ Educ + ECSUsed | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
AffordCostDKMigEveruUsedECSFE       <- feols(AffordCostDK ~ FrenchYN + ECSUsed | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
AffordCostDKEveruUsedECSMigXEducFE  <-  feols( AffordCostDK ~ Educ + FrenchYN + ECSUsed+ Educ*FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)



modelsummary(list(
#"Have no idea of the price by education level"                              = AffordCostDKEduc,                  
"Have no idea of the price by education level with FE"                      = AffordCostDKEducFE,                
#"Have no idea of the price by migration status"                             = AffordCostDKMig,                   
"Have no idea of the price by migration status with FE"                     = AffordCostDKMigFE,              
"Have no idea of the price by Educ control for migration status with FE"    = AffordCostDKEducMigFE,            
"Have no idea of the price by Educ controlling for use with FE"             = AffordCostDKEducEveruUsedECSFE,    
"Have no idea of the price by migration status controlling for use with FE" = AffordCostDKMigEveruUsedECSFE,     
"Have no idea of the price interaction Migration and Educ with FE"          = AffordCostDKEveruUsedECSMigXEducFE 
), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave" ),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Probability to have no idea of the cost of a place in crèche",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)

Going back to our qualitative evidence, we saw that not knowing the cost of childcare can have asymmetrical consequences depending on socioeconomic status. While high-SES families are confident they can afford the cost, no matter what it is (or nearly), low-SES families will be more reluctant to apply because they "cannot end up with another bill they cannot pay".

Running the regressions (see \@ref(Appendix 3) for the detailed regression table), we see that there is a significant negative impact of no knowing the costs on ECS intention (p\< 0.0005), even after controlling for Education level, Migration background, and Activity. As expected given the figures below, none of the interactions with migration background nor education level is significant.

Relatedly, low-SES mothers were also significantly less likely to know the ECS costs are reduced by subsidies, even after controlling for past ECS use (% low-SES = `r KnowsSubNULow`, % high-SES = `r KnowsSubNUHigh`, p\<0.001)

```{r,  LinearSubsidies,echo = FALSE}

modelsummary(list(
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Educ" = KnowsSubsidiesEduc,  
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Educ with FE" = KnowsSubsidiesEducFE,  
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Mig" = KnowsSubsidiesMig,   
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Educ and Mig" = KnowsSubsidiesEducMig, 
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by Educ and ever used" = KnowsSubsidiesEducUsed,
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies by mig and ever used " = KnowsSubsidiesMigUsed, 
"Knows that the price is reduce through subsidies EducXMig " = KnowsSubsidiesEducXMig
), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave" ),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Probability to know that the price of crèche is reduced through subsidies",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)


```

### Relationship between knowing that ECS cost is reduced through subsidies and intention to use ECS

Running the regressions (see \@ref(Appendix 4) for the detailed regression table), we see that there is a significant negative impact of not knowing that ECS cost is reduced through subsidies on ECS intention (p\< 0.0005), even after controlling for Education level, Migration background, and Activity. While the interaction between not knowing about the subsidies and migration background is not significant, the one with education level is.

```{r GraphIntentionSubsidiesEduc, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by knowledge that ECS costs are reduced through subsidies"}

  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=as.factor(AffordSubsidies1or0)),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = as.factor(AffordSubsidies1or0), y = Intention1or0*1000) ,
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  stat_summary(aes(x = as.factor(AffordSubsidies1or0), y = Intention1or0*1000, color = Educ3) ,
               fun.data = "mean_se",

                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
xlab("Knows that ECS cost is reduced through subsidies") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+

  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+

# Parents's perceptions and their relationship to ECS use intentions

## Accessibility

On the one hand, on average, as predicted by the qualitative fieldwork, low-SES women significantly tend to think that accessing a place in ECS is easier than high-SES women do, but perceived accessibility does not seem to play much in ECS use intentions (see Appendix 5 for regression analyses):

We observe a similar trend if we take an alternative measurement of ECS perceived norms: the amount of family and friends that think that using ECS is bad for children. ## ECS returns

However, for a related belief, the one in ECS returns (i.e., believing that if your child is in ECS, she will have better outcomes later), we observe a very different story. While parents believing more in ECS returns are still more likely to plan to use ECS, low-SES parents tend to believe MORE in ECS returns (see details in Appendix 8).

## Perceived monetary and non monetary costs of using childcare versus staying at home

While high-SES parents' intention to use ECS is very little sensitive to perceived costs of these structures, it is not the case for low-SES parents. The latter seem reluctant to apply if the perceived costs are too high.

Again, we observe the pattern previously mentioned for non monetary costs, and the pattern is very similar across non monetary cost types (see details in Appendix 9). High-SES mothers are more likely to perceive high costs of staying at home to take care of their child than their less affluent counterparts, be it on opportunity costs, well-being, or career. And again, mothers that perceive higher costs of staying at home to take care of their child are more likely to want to use ECS afterbirth. This tend is the most salient for opportunity costs and costs on career.

It has to be noted that While mothers born in France are significantly more prone to perceive non monetary costs of staying at home compared to mothers born abroad, the dummy being born in France or not is significant when we predict intention to use ECS based on perceived non monetary costs. However, the dummy AsiaOrMENA or else is: mothers that are born in MENA or Asia are less likely to want to use ECS while the perceived non monetary costs are kept constant, and so are low-educated mothers across all non monetary cost types.

We see different patterns according to ECS types (which is good for internal validity!), and informal care types (see details in Appendix 10). Overall, trust in ECS types significantly predicts intention to use ECS, especially for trust in crèche where the slope is the steepest. While for informal care, we globally see no effect in trust in this type of care on intention to use ECS (see Appendix.

## Perceived Intensity of ECS Needed

Low-SES mothers are likely to need fewer hours than more affluent counterparts. This is the case for low-educated mothers compared to high-educated mothers. Turning to migration background, mothers from MENA and Asia declare needing fewer hours of ECS than others (no difference between mothers born in France and mothers born in remaining world regions).



```{r ECSNeedSES, echo = FALSE,message=FALSE, fig.cap="Intensity of ECS needed by SES"}


 Educ =  data_full %>% filter(ECSNeed != "Ne sait pas encore") %>% 
  mutate(ECSNeed = as.numeric(ECSNeed)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= Educ ,y=ECSNeed, fill = Educ))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_cl_boot", geom = "pointrange")

 
 
 Migration =  data_full %>% filter(ECSNeed != "Ne sait pas encore") %>% 
  mutate(ECSNeed = as.numeric(ECSNeed)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= BirthPlace3 ,y=ECSNeed, fill = BirthPlace3))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_cl_boot", geom = "pointrange")


grid <- plot_grid(
  Educ,
  Migration,
  ncol = 2
)

combine <- plot_grid(
  grid,
  ncol = 1,
  # rel_heights values control vertical title margins
  rel_heights = c( 1,0.1)
)

ggdraw(combine)+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust = 1),
        #plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 1, 0), "cm"))


```

The lower the perceived intensity of ECS needed, the lower the intention to use ECS. Note that mothers that have part-time need for ECS are significantly less likely to plan to use ECS than mothers that need ECS full-time, although drop-in daycare centers (halte-garderies) exist for this very specific need. When looking at the distribution with a dummy for whether the mother knew drop-in daycare or not, we cannot detect any significant difference except the fact that mothers that would never need ECS and even less likely to want to use ECS if they knew drop-in daycare (it might reflect more informed choices). 

Figures are very similar across other measures of SES (migration background), except the fact for mothers from MENA and Asia: when they have part-time ECS needs, they are significantly less likely to plan to use ECS than other mothers with the same needs.

# Resources

## Informal care available


Mothers born in France or in MENA or Asia and low-educated mother can access more informal care on average than others.

```{r InformalSES, fig.cap="Access to informal care by SES"}
 violin <- data_full %>%
  filter(!is.na(AccessInformalCare) & AccessInformalCare != "Je ne sais pas encore") %>% 
  mutate(AccessInformalCare = as.numeric(AccessInformalCare)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= BirthPlace3 ,y=AccessInformalCareFulltime1or0, fill = BirthPlace3))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  labs(y="Probability to access informal care", 
       x = "Birth place of mothers")


 violin2 <-  data_full %>%
  filter(!is.na(AccessInformalCare) & AccessInformalCare != "Je ne sais pas encore") %>% 
  mutate(AccessInformalCare = as.numeric(AccessInformalCare)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= Educ ,y=AccessInformalCareAMAP, fill = Educ))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  ylab("Probability to access informal care")
 
 

grid <- plot_grid(
  violin,
  violin2,
  ncol = 2
)

combine <- plot_grid(
  grid,
  ncol = 1,
  # rel_heights values control vertical title margins
  rel_heights = c( 1,0.1)
)

ggdraw(combine)+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust = 1),
        #plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 1, 0), "cm"))


```

Having access to informal care is negatively correlated with the intention to use ECS afterbirth. This is slightly more true for low-educated mothers, and for mothers from MENA and Asia.

# "Cognitive" variables

## Present bias 


Mothers born in France and highly-educated mothers have a higher tendency to choose more important reward more distant in time compared to others.

```{r DiscountSES, fig.cap= " Discount rate by SES"}

 violin <- data_full %>%  filter(DiscountRate != "Je ne sais pas") %>%
  mutate(DiscountRate = as.numeric(DiscountRate)) %>%

  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+

       x = "Birth place of mothers")

  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  ylab("Probability to value education")+
  labs(y="Temporal discounting rate", 
       x = "Education level")

## Informal reciprocity


While mothers born in France already take more care of children of others compared to others, highly-educated mothers are just as likely to access this kind of resources compared to others.

```{r RecpSES, fig.cap="Informal reciprocity by SES"}

 violin <- data_full %>% filter(InformalReciprocity != "Je ne souhaite pas répondre") %>% 
  mutate(InformalReciprocity = as.numeric(InformalReciprocity)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= BirthPlace3 ,y=InformalReciprocity, fill = BirthPlace3))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  labs(y="Amount of informal care already given by mothers to other children", 
       x = "Birth place of mothers")

 violin2 <-  data_full  %>% filter(InformalReciprocity != "Je ne souhaite pas répondre") %>% 
  mutate(InformalReciprocity = as.numeric(InformalReciprocity)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= Educ ,y=InformalReciprocity, fill = Educ))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  ylab("Amount of informal care already given by mothers to other children")
 


grid <- plot_grid(
  violin,
  violin2,
  ncol = 2
)

combine <- plot_grid(
  grid,
  ncol = 1,
  # rel_heights values control vertical title margins
  rel_heights = c( 1,0.1)
)

ggdraw(combine)+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust = 1),
        #plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 1, 0), "cm"))

```

We find no effect of informal reciprocity effect on ECS intention neither by education nor by migration background: Mothers that already take care of children of others are not less likely to want to use ECS compared to other mothers.

```{r InformalReciprocity,  fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by Informal reciprocity and SES"}

data_full%>%

  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=InformalReciprocity ,fill=BirthPlace3),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = InformalReciprocity, y = Intention1or0*1000),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  stat_summary(aes(x = InformalReciprocity, y = Intention1or0*1000, color = BirthPlace3),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
xlab("The mother already takes care of children of others") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+
  geom_smooth(aes(y=Intention1or0*1000,x=as.numeric(InformalReciprocity),color=BirthPlace3), alpha = 0.1,
              method = "lm_robust")+
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("No", "For emergencies", "From time to time"))

```

## Structural factors

### Coverage rate

We find evidence of information asymmetry related to structural factors: while the coverage rate does not change low-educated mothers' intention to use ECS, the lower the coverage rate, the less highly-educated mothers plan to use ECS. 

```{r plotIntend,results='asis',warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,fig.cap="Intention to use formal childcare correlates with higher the ECEC cover rate, but only for those with higher education",fig.pos="h"}

PremiersPas <- read.csv("../Data/BaselinePremiersPas.csv")

bw <- 2 * IQR(PremiersPas$TAUXCOUV_COM) / length(PremiersPas$TAUXCOUV_COM)^(1/3)

ECEC <- ggplot(PremiersPas %>% filter(TAUXCOUV_COM<=100))+
  stat_summary_bin(aes(y=as.numeric(ECSPlanTo),x=TAUXCOUV_COM,color=Educ),
                   binwidth=bw,fun.data = "mean_se",fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(.975)),
                   size=.4)+
  geom_smooth(aes(y=as.numeric(ECSPlanTo),x=TAUXCOUV_COM,color=Educ),
              method = "lm_robust",formula = y ~ splines::bs(x, df=3)
              )+ylim(c(0,1.25))+
  geom_histogram(aes(x=TAUXCOUV_COM,y=..count../200,fill=Educ),alpha=.2,binwidth=bw)+
   theme_bw()+scale_color_manual("Education:",values =cbPalette[c(4,6,8)],labels=c("High school or Lower", "Higher education"))+
  scale_fill_manual("Education:",values =cbPalette[c(4,6,8)],labels=c("High school or lower", "Higher education"))+
  scale_shape("Education:")+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 1, 0), "cm"))+
  scale_x_continuous("ECEC cover rate in the city",n.breaks=21)+
  ylab("Share intentending to use ECEC")+
  labs(title="Intention to use childcare",
       subtitle="by ECEC cover rate and education")

legend <- get_legend(ECEC)

Work <- ggplot(PremiersPas %>% filter(TAUXCOUV_COM<=100) %>% mutate(WorkPlanTo=ifelse(WorkPlanTo==TRUE,1,0)))+
  stat_summary_bin(aes(y=as.numeric(WorkPlanTo),x=TAUXCOUV_COM,color=Educ),
                   binwidth=bw,fun.data = "mean_se",fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(.975)),
                   size=.4)+
  geom_smooth(aes(y=as.numeric(WorkPlanTo),x=TAUXCOUV_COM,color=Educ),
              method = "lm_robust",formula = y ~ splines::bs(x, df=3)
              )+
  geom_histogram(aes(x=TAUXCOUV_COM,y=..count../200,fill=Educ),alpha=.2,binwidth=bw)+
   theme_bw()+scale_color_manual("Education:",values =cbPalette[c(4,6,8)],labels=c("High school or Lower", "Higher education"))+
  scale_fill_manual("Education:",values =cbPalette[c(4,6,8)],labels=c("High school or lower", "Higher education"))+ylim(c(0,1.25))+
  scale_shape("Education:")+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 1, 0), "cm"))+
  scale_x_continuous("ECEC cover rate in the city",n.breaks=21)+
  ylab("Share intentending to work")+
  labs(title="Intention to work",
       subtitle="by ECEC cover rate and education")

legend <- get_legend(ECEC)



grid <- plot_grid(
  ECEC+theme(legend.position="none"),
  Work+theme(legend.position="none"),
  ncol = 2
)

combine <- plot_grid(
  grid,legend,
  ncol = 1,
  # rel_heights values control vertical title margins
  rel_heights = c( 1,0.1)
)

ggdraw(combine)+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust = 1),
        
        #plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 1, 0), "cm"))



```

```{r plotIntendUse,results='asis',warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,fig.cap="Intention to use formal childcare correlates with higher the ECEC cover rate, but only for those with higher education",fig.pos="h"}

                   binwidth=bw,fun.data = "mean_se",fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(.975)),
                   size=.4)+
  geom_smooth(aes(y=as.numeric(ECSPlanTo),x=TAUXCOUV_COM,color=Educ),
              method = "lm_robust",formula = y ~ splines::bs(x, df=3)
              )+ylim(c(0,1.25))+
  geom_histogram(aes(x=TAUXCOUV_COM,y=..count../200,fill=Educ),alpha=.2,binwidth=bw)+
   theme_bw()+scale_color_manual("Education:",values =cbPalette[c(4,6,8)],labels=c("High school or Lower", "Higher education"))+
  scale_fill_manual("Education:",values =cbPalette[c(4,6,8)],labels=c("High school or lower", "Higher education"))+
  scale_shape("Education:")+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 1, 0), "cm"))+
  scale_x_continuous("ECEC cover rate in the city",n.breaks=21)+
  ylab("Share intentending to use ECEC")+
  labs(title="Intention to use childcare",
       subtitle="by ECEC cover rate and education")




```



## Access to a computer

Mothers born in France and highly-educated mothers can access a computer more (nearly all of them) compared to others .

```{r ComputerSES, fig.cap="Access to a computer by SES"}

 violin <- data_full %>% 
  mutate(Computer1or0 = as.numeric(Computer1or0)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= BirthPlace3 ,y=Computer1or0, fill = BirthPlace3))+

  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  labs(y="Probability to access a computer", 
       x = "Birth place of mothers")

 violin2 <-  data_full  %>% 
  mutate(Computer1or0 = as.numeric(Computer1or0)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= Educ ,y=Computer1or0, fill = Educ))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  ylab("Probability to access a computer")
 


grid <- plot_grid(

)

combine <- plot_grid(

# Months of pregnancy

Surprisingly, we find a pattern in ECS intention according to month of pregnancy and level of education: it starts diverging after 4 months of pregnancy. We do not find the same pattern according to migration background.

```{r MonthsPregnancy,  fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by pregnancy month and SES"}

xlab("Months of pregnancy") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+

varToKeep <- forGRF %>% summarise_all(~sum(is.na(.))<100) %>% select_if(.==TRUE) %>% names()
forGRF <- forGRF %>% select(varToKeep)
OrderedVar <- forGRF %>% select_if(is.ordered) %>% names()
TFVAR <- forGRF %>% select_if(is.logical) %>% names()
forGRF <- forGRF %>% mutate_at(vars(OrderedVar),~as.numeric(.)) %>% mutate_at(vars(TFVAR),~ifelse(.==TRUE,1,0))

dummified <- model.matrix(~.,forGRF) %>% as.data.frame() %>% select(-c("(Intercept)"))
X=dummified %>% select(-c(Intention1or0,blocksMatWave))# %>% as.matrix(.)

RF_Base <- regression_forest(
  X=X %>% as.matrix(.),
  dummified$Intention1or0,
  num.trees = 10000,
  sample.weights = NULL,
  clusters = dummified$blocksMatWave,
  equalize.cluster.weights = TRUE,
  sample.fraction = 0.5,
  mtry = min(ceiling(sqrt(ncol(dummified %>% select(-Intention1or0,blocksMatWave))) + 20), ncol(dummified %>% select(-Intention1or0,blocksMatWave))),
  min.node.size = 5,
  honesty = TRUE,
  honesty.fraction = 0.5,
  honesty.prune.leaves = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  imbalance.penalty = 0,
  ci.group.size = 2,
  tune.parameters = "all",
  tune.num.trees = 500,
  tune.num.reps = 1000,
  tune.num.draws = 10000,
  compute.oob.predictions = TRUE,
  num.threads = NULL,
  seed = 03092023
)


varimp.Y <- variable_importance(RF_Base)

keep <- colnames(X)[order(varimp.Y, decreasing = TRUE)[1:20]]

test_calibration(RF_Base)

## Balance checks

Only differences found (0.10 level):
- Control-T1: We have slightly more mothers that want to work after birth, that value socialization, are less present orientated, and that trust daycare center (0.05) in the *control* group compared to T1.
- Control-T2: We have slightly more mothers that are already active, that are born in France,  are less present orientated,and that value socialization in the *control* group compared to T2. Mothers in T2 value obedience a little bit more.
- T1-T2: We have slightly more mothers that values obedience in T2 compared to T1. 
```{r BalanceContT1, fig.width= 30 }

tabVar <- MainDB  %>% filter(Assignment == "Control" | Assignment == "T1") %>% filter(ResponseId ==1) %>% 
   mutate(
     SingleMum1or0 = ifelse(SingleMum == TRUE, 1, 0),
     CoupleCohabiting1or0 = ifelse(CoupleCohabiting == TRUE, 1, 0),

#%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%#######-##-
##### Import and clean the raw survey database %%%%%%%%%%%##
#####%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%#######-###-


##Import data_full, the baseline dataset
data_full <- read_csv("../Data/BaselinePremiersPas.csv")


##Import data_tot_clean with excluded participants (the ones that were undocumented or did not leave their phone number)
data_tot_clean <- read_csv("../Data/Full_dataset_PremiersPas_with_undocumented.csv") 



#convert relevant VARIABLES INTO FACTORS
##NB: pour ajouter les stats sur les heures, prendre le dataset du 24/10 et ajouter "'HOUR_1','HOUR_2','HOUR_3','HOUR_4',"
names <- c("ResponseId", "SurveyorId", "MaternityWard", "Dep", "CodePostal", "DateArrival",
           "DateArrival2", "SansPapier", "Relationship", "Language", "Preg7Less", "SmokePreg", 
           "BreastFeedIntend", "OrderedEduc", "Educ", "Act3", "FmlyIncome", "Income", "ECSType7", "FrenchYN", 
           "Intention.x", "ECSUsed", "ECSNeed", "ECSIdealAgeEntry", "AffordSubsidies", "AffordNMCostWB", "AffordOppCost", 
           "AffordNMCostCareer", "DiscountRate", "AccessEasy", "AccessHours", "AccessInformalCare", "Norms", "NormsOpposedDK",
           "LikertAccessInfo", "LikertReturnHK", "LikertAccessSoc", "TrustFam", "TrustFriend", "TrustAssMat", "TrustCreche", 
           "DeprivClothes", "DeprivFood", "DeprivBills", "DeprivHolidays", "DeprivHousing", "InformalReciprocity", 
           "LevelComprehensionExPost", "LevelExpressionExPost", "LevelInfoSubExPost", "LevelPartnerAnsweredExPost", 
           "ComputerYN", "AgeSup32", "BirthPlace", "BirthPlace2", "OrderedEduc2", "Occupation", "Occupation2", 
           "AfterBirthOccupation", "NUMCOM", "COM", "REG", "HighLowECEC", "Educ2", "Intention.y", "UsedECEC", "IntendUse",
           "Assignment", "Which_wave", "labels", "blocksMatWaveStrata", "blocksMatWave", "code_commune", "code_departement"
           
)

data_full[,names] <- lapply(data_full[,names] , factor)

#convert relevant VARIABLES INTO numerical ones


names_numerical <- c("AgeChild1", "AgeChild2", "AgeChild3", "AgeChild4", "AgeChild5", "AgeChild6", "AgeChild7", "AgeChild8",
                     "Age", "KnowsCreche", "KnowsCrecheA", "KnowsCrechePub", "KnowsAssMat", "KnowsNotYet", "KnowsJE", "KnowsAutre",
                     "KnowsPartage", "KnowsHG", "KnowsNounou", "KnowsNothing", "WantCreche", "WantCrecheA", "WantAssMat", "WantJE", 
                     "WantAutre", "WantPartage", "WantHG", "WantNounou", "KnownNbTypeECS", "PregMonth", "BreastFeedLength",
                     "BreastFeedIntend1or0", "AffordSubsidies1or0", "NormsOpposedN", "LikertReturnHK1or0", "TrustCreche1or0",
                     "AffordCost", "NumberChildren", "AccessImpossible", "AccessHard", "AccessHardtoImpossible", "AccessEasy1or0", 
                     "AccessEasyDK", "AccessNotHours", "AccessNotInformalCare", "AccessInformalCareAMAP", "ValGenerosity", 
                     "ValIndependence", "ValSocialisation", "ValObedience", "ValEducation", "ValDK", "ValImagination", "ValNone", 
                     "WorkBefore", "FmilyEarnLessThan2500", "EarnLessThan1500", "Intention1or0", "CODDEP", "CODREG", "PTOT", 
                     "TAUXCOUV_COM", "TAUXCOUV_EPCI", "TAUXCOUV_DEP", "TAUXCOUV_NAT", "n", "strata", "group_id", "prixMoyen", 
                     "PrixMedian", "surfaceReelleBati", "PrixMoyenM2Bati")
data_full[,names_numerical] <- lapply(data_full[,names_numerical] , as.numeric)

# Order relevant variables


data_full <- data_full %>%  mutate(
         OrderedEduc=factor(OrderedEduc, levels =
             c("No school", "9-11", "Brevet", "CAP", "Bac", "Bac +2", "Bac + 3", "Bac + 4/5", "+ Bac+5"), ordered = TRUE),
         Income = factor(Income, 
                         levels = c("NSP","- 500","500-700", "1000-1500", 
                                    "1500-2000", "2000-2500", "2500-3000", "3000-4500", "4500-5000",  "5000-6000", "Ne veut pas répondre" ), ordered = TRUE),
         FmlyIncome = factor(FmlyIncome,

## Appendix {-}: Regression table of the relationship between Number of ECS known and Intention {#Appendix}

```{r modIntentionNECSKnown,echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

# Relationship between Number of ECS known and Intention


IntentionECSKnown            <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ KnownNbTypeECS, data = data_full)
IntentionECSKnownFE          <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ KnownNbTypeECS| blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)      
IntentionECSKnownEduc        <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ KnownNbTypeECS + Educ | blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )     
IntentionECSKnownEducMig     <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ KnownNbTypeECS + Educ + FrenchYN| blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )
IntentionECSKnownEducMigAct  <- feols(Intention1or0 ~ KnownNbTypeECS + Educ + FrenchYN + Active| blocksMatWave , data = data_full, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave )



modelsummary(list(
"Intention by ECS known"                                                               = IntentionECSKnown,           
"Intention by ECS known with FE"                                                       = IntentionECSKnownFE,         
"Intention by ECS known controlling for Educ with FE"                                  = IntentionECSKnownEduc,       
"Intention by ECS known controlling for Educ and migration background with FE"         = IntentionECSKnownEducMig,    
"Intention by ECS known controlling for Educ, migration background and activity with FE"         =IntentionECSKnownEducMigAct 
), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs",  "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: WardxWave" ),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Inention and number of ECS known",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)


```

### Trust in private chidminders

1. First, low-SES parents are less likely to trust daycare centers. This time, both dummy being born in France or not and being born in Asia or MENA or not are significant with not controls, and then stay significant at least at the 10 percent level. ECS used is never significant. We explain low variance with these models.

```{r modTrustAssMatSES,echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}
TrustAssMatEduc        <-feols(as.numeric(TrustAssMat) ~ Educ, data = data_full)

### Trust in friends

2. Second, mothers that trust friends less are just as likely as others to intend to use ECS (which is againg super reassuring for internal validity), while we see significant differences in that according to SES. ### Idenpendance

Mothers born in France and highly-educated mothers have a higher probability to value independence as an important skill to acquire before preschool.

```{r IndepSES, fig.cap="Probability to value obedience by SES"}

 violin <- data_full %>% 
  mutate(ValIndependence = as.numeric(ValIndependence)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= BirthPlace3 ,y=ValIndependence, fill = BirthPlace3))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  labs(y="Probability to value independence", 
       x = "Birth place of mothers")

 violin2 <-  data_full  %>% 
  mutate(ValIndependence = as.numeric(ValIndependence)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= Educ ,y=ValIndependence, fill = Educ))+
  geom_violin()+
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "pointrange")+
  ylab("Probability to value independence")
 


grid <- plot_grid(
  violin,
  violin2,
  ncol = 2
)

combine <- plot_grid(
  grid,
  ncol = 1,
  # rel_heights values control vertical title margins
  rel_heights = c( 1,0.1)
)

ggdraw(combine)+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust = 1),
        #plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 1, 0), "cm"))

```

Valuing independance is slightly related to increased ECS intention only for highly-educated mothers. 

```{r ValueIndepIntention,  fig.cap="Intention to use ECS by value independance and SES"}


data_full%>%

         ValIndependence = as.factor(ValIndependence)) %>%

  geom_bar(aes(x=ValIndependence ,fill=Educ),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = ValIndependence, y = Intention1or0*1000),
               fun.data = "mean_se",
               fun.args = list(mult = qnorm(0.975)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +

  geom_bar(aes(x=BreastFeedLength ,fill=Educ),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  geom_smooth(aes(y=Intention1or0*1000,x=as.numeric(BreastFeedLength),color=Educ), alpha = 0.1,
              method = "loess")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+
xlab("Intended lenght of breastfeeding period")

  
data_full%>% filter(as.numeric(BreastFeedLength) < 30) %>% 
  mutate(Intention1or0 = as.numeric(Intention1or0),
         ValGenerosity = as.factor(ValGenerosity)) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x=BreastFeedLength ,fill=BirthPlace3),position="stack",alpha=.2)+
  geom_smooth(aes(y=Intention1or0*1000,x=as.numeric(BreastFeedLength),color=BirthPlace3), alpha = 0.1,
              method = "loess")+ 
  ylab("Number of observations")+
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1000, name = "Pr (Intention)"))+
xlab("Intended lenght of breastfeeding period")

```{r modDeprivedSES,echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

DeprivHolidaysMA          <-feols(as.numeric(DeprivHolidays) ~ BirthPlace3 | blocksMatWave, data = DeprivHolidays, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
DeprivHolidaysEducMA      <-feols(as.numeric(DeprivHolidays) ~ Educ + BirthPlace3| blocksMatWave, data = DeprivHolidays, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
DeprivHolidaysEducUsed    <-feols(as.numeric(DeprivHolidays) ~ Educ + ECSUsed | blocksMatWave, data = DeprivHolidays, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
DeprivHolidaysMigUsedEduc <-feols(as.numeric(DeprivHolidays) ~ BirthPlace3 + Educ + ECSUsed | blocksMatWave, data = DeprivHolidays, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
DeprivHolidaysEducXMA     <-feols(as.numeric(DeprivHolidays) ~ Educ + BirthPlace3 + ECSUsed + Educ*BirthPlace3| blocksMatWave, data = DeprivHolidays, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)



modelsummary(list(
"Exposure to deprivation by Educ"                    = DeprivHolidaysEduc,

), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",

## Appendix {-} Past ECS Use

1. First, low-SES parents and mothers not born in France nor in MENA/Asia are less likely to have already used ECS when it is not their first child.

```{r modECSUseSES,echo = FALSE,message=FALSE}

Primipare =data_full %>% filter(Primipare == "FALSE")


ECSUseEduc           <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ Educ | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
ECSUseEduc3          <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ i(Educ3, ref = "Undergrad") | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave) 
ECSUseMig            <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ FrenchYN | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
ECSUseMENA           <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ BirthPlace3 | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
ECSUseActive         <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ Active | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
ECSUseEducMigAct     <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ Educ + FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
ECSUseEducMig        <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Active| blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
ECSUseEducXMig       <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ Educ + FrenchYN + Educ*FrenchYN| blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
ECSUseEducXMENA       <- feols(as.numeric(ECSUsed) ~ Educ + BirthPlace3 + Educ*BirthPlace3| blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
Intention                      <- feols(as.numeric(Intention1or0) ~ ECSUsed | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave) 
IntentionCont                  <- feols(as.numeric(Intention1or0) ~ ECSUsed + FrenchYN + Educ | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave) 
IntentionContAct               <- feols(as.numeric(Intention1or0) ~ ECSUsed + FrenchYN + Educ + Active | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave) 
IntentionInterEduc             <- feols(as.numeric(Intention1or0) ~ interaction(ECSUsed, Educ3) | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
IntentionInterMENA             <- feols(as.numeric(Intention1or0) ~ interaction(ECSUsed, BirthPlace3) | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
IntentionCont                  <- feols(as.numeric(Intention1or0) ~ ECSUsed + FrenchYN + Educ | blocksMatWave, data = Primipare, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave) 



modelsummary(list(
"(1)"           = ECSUseEduc,  
"(2)"           = ECSUseEduc3,  
"(3)"           = ECSUseMig,  
"(4)"           = ECSUseMENA,  
"(5)"           = ECSUseActive,  
"(6)"           = ECSUseEducMig, 
"(7)"           = ECSUseEducMigAct,
"(8)"           = ECSUseEducXMig,  
"(9)  Intention"          = Intention,
"(10) Intention"          = IntentionCont,
"(11) Intention"          = IntentionContAct, 
"(12) Intention"          = IntentionInterEduc,
"(13) Intention"          = IntentionInterMENA 

), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
   estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
   gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: blocksMatWave"),
   stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
   title="Valuing socialization",
   notes=list("",
              "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis"),
   output = 'flextable',
   escape = TRUE
)

```

MigEducUsed <-feols(as.numeric(LikertAccessSoc) ~ BirthPlace3 + ECSUsed + Educ | blocksMatWave, data = LikertInfo, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)
EducXMig    <-feols(as.numeric(LikertAccessSoc) ~ Educ + BirthPlace3 + Educ*BirthPlace3| blocksMatWave, data = LikertInfo, cluster = ~ blocksMatWave)


modelsummary(list(
"Educ"                    = Educ,    
"Educ with FE"            = EducFE,  
"Mig"                     = Mig, 
"Educ and Mig"            = EducMig, 
"Educ and ever used"      = EducUsed,
"mig and ever used "      = MigUsed,
"mig educ and ever used " = MigEducUsed,
"EducXMig "               = EducXMig
), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: blocksMatWave" ),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Access to informational resources and SES",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE)




```

## Appendix {-} Values - Perceived monetary and non monetary costs of using childcare versus staying at home by income


While high-SES parents' intention to use ECS is very little sensitive to perceived costs of these structures, it is not the case for low-SES parents. The latter seem reluctant to apply if the perceived costs are too high.The slope is less steep as income rise


```{r costIncome, fig.cap="Intention by perceived cost and Educ"}


data_full %>% filter(Income4 != "Ne veut pas répondre" & Income4 != "NSP" ) %>% 
ggplot(aes(as.numeric(AffordCost), as.numeric(Intention1or0), color = as.factor(Income4)))+
  stat_smooth(method="glm", formula=y~x,
alpha=0.2, size=2, aes(fill = Income4)) +
xlab("Perceived cost of childcare") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ facet_wrap(~as.factor(Income4))
```
For family income:

```{r costFamIncome, fig.cap="Intention by perceived cost and Educ"}


data_full %>% filter(FmlyIncome6  != "Ne veut pas répondre" & FmlyIncome6  != "NSP" & FmlyIncome6 != is.na(FmlyIncome6 ) ) %>% 
ggplot(aes(as.numeric(AffordCost), as.numeric(Intention1or0), color = as.factor(FmlyIncome6 )))+
  stat_smooth(method="glm", formula=y~x,
alpha=0.2, size=2, aes(fill = FmlyIncome6 )) +
xlab("Perceived cost of childcare") + ylab("Pr (Intention)")+ facet_wrap(~as.factor(FmlyIncome6))
```

Again, we observe the pattern previously mentioned for non monetary costs, and the pattern is very similar across non monetary cost types (see details in Appendix 9). High-SES mothers are more likely to perceive high costs of staying at home to take care of their child than their less affluent counterparts, be it on opportunity costs, well-being, or career. And again, mothers that perceive higher costs of staying at home to take care of their child are more likely to want to use ECS afterbirth. This tend is the most salient for opportunity costs and costs on career.

It has to be noted that While mothers born in France are significantly more prone to perceive non monetary costs of staying at home compared to mothers born abroad, the dummy being born in France or not is significant when we predict intention to use ECS based on perceived non monetary costs. However, the dummy AsiaOrMENA or else is: mothers that are born in MENA or Asia are less likely to want to use ECS while the perceived non monetary costs are kept constant, and so are low-educated mothers across all non monetary cost types.
